hints: Look very carefully at the difference in wording between 1 cell repair and 2 cell replacement. One means fixing an existing cell, the other means making a brand new cell.
Remember the core job of mitosis is to make new identical cells by cell division. Ask yourself for each of 1 to 5, does this process need new cells to be made?
walkthrough:
**Recall what mitosis is for**

Great start. Mitosis is nuclear division followed by cell division to make two genetically identical cells.

So a drug that stops mitosis stops the production of all new cells.

**Check 2, 3, 4 and 5 - all need new cells**

Cell replacement (2) needs mitosis to replace old or dead cells, like skin or blood cells.

Stem cells (3) divide by mitosis to self-renew and to produce specialised cells, so their number is affected.

Tissue repair (4) needs lots of mitosis to fill a wound with new cells.

Tumour formation (5) is uncontrolled mitosis, so stopping mitosis will directly stop tumours growing.

**Spot why 1 is different**

Cell repair does not mean making a new cell. It means repairing damage inside an existing cell, for example repairing membranes or proteins.

That does not need mitosis, so it is not affected. That leaves 2, 3, 4 and 5 only, which is option D.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 1. Cell repair is fixing an existing cell and does not require mitosis.
options.B: Incorrect because it misses 4 and 5. Both tissue repair and tumour formation depend on making new cells by mitosis.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes 1 and misses 2 and 3. Cell replacement and stem cell renewal need mitosis, while cell repair does not.
options.D: Correct. 2, 3, 4 and 5 all require production of new cells by mitosis, while 1 cell repair does not.
